messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Miller <sarah.miller@NimbusHealth.com>, Jack Turner <jack.turner@medicalai.co>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>

Subject: Draft pricing & surge safety-net options for Nimbus Health

Sarah / Jack —

Thanks for the call this morning. Attached is a short draft that lays out the two paths we discussed for Hosted API billing: 1) a straightforward quarterly commit with a firm minimum spend and a higher on-demand overage rate; or 2) a commit + temporary soft-burst buffer that covers early spikes and tapers to the standard overage after a grace window.

High-level bullets:
- Commit: monthly committed spend (tokens) with a 12-month term; invoiced monthly.
- Minimum guarantee: 80% of the commit billed as minimum if underutilized (true-up at year end).
- On-demand overage: when commit exhausted, requests fall back to on-demand at a per-token rate that is ~2.5x the commit rate.
- Soft-burst buffer: optional 10–20% of commit as a temporary buffer for first 60–90 days, billed at commit rate; after buffer used, on-demand overage applies.

I attached a simple examples workbook that walks through three usage months (steady, spike, low). Please review and tell us which model you prefer — we can surface a concrete term sheet.

Attachments: nimbus_pricing_examples.xlsx (spreadsheet), burst_policy_spec.md (policy notes)

Next step: can we schedule a 30-minute procurement/deck review this week? I can make time Thursday afternoon PT.

Best,
Ben Carter

Ben —

Thanks for the deck and the examples. A couple of clarifying questions before we lock in an internal procurement review:
1) The "minimum guarantee" language — does that mean we pay 80% of committed spend even if we use less, or is that a true-up at the end of the year where unused tokens are credited?
2) For the soft-burst buffer: is that a fixed % that resets each month, or a one-time allowance that gets consumed?
3) The on-demand multiple (~2.5x) — can we see a capped-cost scenario for a 10x spike month? Procurement will want a worst-case monthly cap tied to a multiple of commit, or a dollar cap, to avoid runaway charges.

Also looping procurement: procurement@NimbusHealth.com — Sarah, Jack and I need the example you mentioned showing a month with a big spike vs the commit baseline. Can you include an example with 10x peak for one week and how the invoice would read?

Appreciate it — happy to do the call on Thursday if you send over the updated examples first.

Thanks,
Sarah Miller
Head of Data Ops, Nimbus Health
sarah.miller@NimbusHealth.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Miller <sarah.miller@NimbusHealth.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Jack Turner <jack.turner@medicalai.co>
Date: 2026-06-21T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft pricing & surge safety-net options for Nimbus Health

Sarah — good questions. Quick answers first, details below and in the updated spreadsheet I've attached.

Short answers:
- Minimum guarantee: billed monthly as 80% of committed monthly spend. Unused tokens do not roll over; instead we apply a year-end true-up reconciliation if the annual committed total is unmet. (We can negotiate a different true-up cadence if needed.)
- Soft-burst buffer: proposed as a one-time onboarding buffer equal to X% of commit that is available for the first N days (not a monthly reset) — this is cleaner for forecasting and avoids recurring uncertainty.
- Capped-cost scenario: we can offer an optional "surge cap" that limits any single month's charge to at most 3.5x the committed monthly charge (including overage) — this would be a negotiated concession for the first 3 months.

Example (from attached workbook):
- Commit: $40k/month (baseline).
- Soft-burst buffer: 15% for first 60 days (i.e., an extra $6k of tokens at commit rate).
- On-demand overage rate: commit per-token rate = $0.00012; on-demand = $0.00030 (2.5x).

Month with 10x peak week: total token usage results in invoice = commit ($40k) + overage on tokens beyond commit+buffer at $0.00030; with a 3.5x surge cap the invoice would be capped at $140k for that month. Without cap the invoice could be ~$180k in the modeled extreme.

Attached: updated nimbus_pricing_examples.xlsx (with capped scenario) and burst_policy_spec.md (policy clauses).

Ben

Subject: Internal: suggested concession language for Nimbus (notes for Irene)

Irene / Ben — quick internal note before we finalize counters:

Proposal for commercial concession to help close. I recommend offering the following, linked to DEAL-4892:
- 12-month committed term at a 10% discount off list commit rates.
- A temporary 15% soft-burst buffer available for the first 90 days post-go-live, billed at commit rate; buffer does not reset monthly.
- A surge-cap option: limit any single month's invoice to 3.5x the committed monthly charge for months 1–3 only.
- Standard true-up at year-end. If Nimbus wants a month-by-month rollover model, we should ask for an additional 2% fee (or reduce discount).

Rationale: gives Nimbus predictability for onboarding spikes while protecting us from sustained overages. If we can sign 12 months at 10% off, we keep gross economics intact.

Ask: Irene, can you approve the 90-day buffer + 10% commit discount? If yes I will draft the concession language for sales/legal to insert into the SOW. If you want to shorten the buffer to 60 days (less exposure) we can do that too.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Field Pricing, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Surge safety-net / minimum guarantee and true-up scenarios for Nimbus Health

All —

Thanks for the thoughtful options. I approve moving forward with an offer tied to 12 months and a commit discount, with two requested changes before we present to procurement:

1) Reduce the soft-burst buffer window from 90 days to 60 days. That gives Nimbus meaningful onboarding protection while limiting our exposure.
2) Include explicit monthly usage reporting and token-level audit logs (daily export) as part of the SOW so Nimbus can reconcile spikes quickly.
3) Offer the surge-cap as a signed option for months 1–2 instead of 1–3; we can extend if usage proves stable.

Ben — please prepare a redlined SOW with the three edits and the sample capped invoice examples. Send to procurement@NimbusHealth.com and include the proposed_contract_redline.docx as the first draft attachment. Legal can review after we get procurement's feedback.

Good work — looks like we're in shape to close given procurement's appetite for predictability.

Best,
Irene Choi
